18K likes, 105 comments - siddharthajoshi on June 19, 2026: "Evenings in Edinburgh are truly magical.

At first, I thought I had simply gotten lucky with the light. But later I learned that skies like these are not uncommon here - and suddenly it made perfect sense why this city has inspired so many writers, artists, and dreamers over the centuries.

What made this walk so special was how quickly everything changed. Every few minutes, the sky seemed to reinvent itself. One horizon glowed with shades of gold, pink, and orange, while the other slowly deepened into an endless blue. It felt as though two different evenings were unfolding at the same time.

There was so much drama in the sky, so much movement and play…

Some places impress you with monuments and history. Edinburgh does that too - but on evenings like this, it’s the sky that steals the show…

Shot on Nikon Z6III ❤️

with @nikonindiaofficial @nikonasia

#Nikoncreators #NikonZseries #NikonIndia
#Nikonmirrorless".

482 likes, 22 comments - siddharthajoshi on October 7, 2026: "5 days behind the wheel of an iconic UAZ (Ulyanovsky Avtomobilny Zavod), white-knuckling through remote mountain passes! 

Born in Soviet times, the UAZ is a legendary off-road icon engineered purely for survival in extreme terrain. With no power steering, no modern electronic safety nets, and heavy manual gear shifts, driving it requires raw physical focus and mechanical intuition. Mastering this Soviet workhorse over steep mountain passes was the ultimate thrill.

Every night brought a fresh view as I slept on a new mountain top or parked just outside an ancient stone village, cooking simple meals and watching movies in the back of the truck. But the highlight of it all was my final night along Sulak Canyon - sleeping right under the open sky and waking up with the rising sun, no plans or agenda, just total freedom.

Beyond the raw driving, what made every single day special was meeting complete strangers along the way - from stopping in remote villages for hot tea to making lifelong friends on the road.

Stepping completely out of my comfort zone behind the wheel turned out to be the adventure of a lifetime.

#dagestan #uaz".

627 likes, 21 comments - siddharthajoshi on October 3, 2026: "My first time here, and I ended up in one of its most rugged, breathtaking, and lesser-explored regions: Dagestan! 

From the moment I landed, @uaz.family handled the entire journey seamlessly - from sorting my e-visa and e-SIM to connecting me with amazing local English-speaking groups in Makhachkala, where I got a front-row seat to the city’s unique history, and it’s insane MMA culture.

Next we spent 5 days hiking high through the Caucasus Mountains - staying at three distinct, pristine campsites (ridge views, alpine plateaus, and river valleys), enjoying gourmet campsite meals by our chef Mohamad, taking hot showers in the wild, and bonding late into the night over delicious local wine and games.

Then came the ultimate highlight: Andreas trusted me with the keys to an iconic Soviet 4×4 UAZ for a multi-day self-driving adventure! Navigating mountain passes, experiencing the legendary hospitality of mountain villages, and camping out solo under the glowing Milky Way was pure magic.

This was truly an adventure of a lifetime. Stay tuned - I’ll be sharing the full story, breakdowns, and all the details of what happened on this wild ride very soon! 🏔️🚘✨

#Dagestan #UAZFamily #Caucasus #uaz".

1,351 likes, 5 comments - siddharthajoshi on September 3, 2026: "You can’t stand ON the North Pole?

It’s not land - it’s just ice, floating on the Arctic Ocean. And the closer you get to 90°N, the less solid ground there is beneath you. At the Pole itself, the ocean floor is 4.2 km down. No land. Just ice, drifting on open water. 

Fun fact: Antarctica is a continent surrounded by ocean. The Arctic is an ocean surrounded by continents. Total opposites.

📍 Svalbard, Norway

#NorthPole #Arctic #Svalbard".

4,465 likes, 19 comments - siddharthajoshi on September 13, 2026: "Why does the iPhone Duo costs so much in India? 

Before assuming it’s just a markup, and possibly some of it is, but frankly most of it comes from the factors below:

- US Base Price: $1,999 pre-tax ➔ ~$2,15,000 post-tax in the US.

- Local Assembly Savings: Apple makes standard iPhones locally in India to save ~17% import duty.

- The CBU Reality: The iPhone Duo’s complex precision engineering (100+ hinge components, new PCB, custom display) requires new assembly tech that isn’t in India yet. 
 
- Taxes & Logistics: Importing it fully built (CBU) triggers heavy Import Duties + 18% GST + Forex buffers, driving up the cost by ₹60,000–₹70,000.

Once local assembly kicks in for future generations, expect those heavy import duties to drop! Or will they?

Drop your thoughts in the comments! 👇

#iphoneduo #iphone #appleevent".
